rationale: ROUND 4 (round 3: REVISE, gated by editquality's jsonb-NULL concern about the verify block). This round changes NO code and NO config — every round-3 objection is answered with a measurement run 2026-08-09 ~12:10Z, several by INDUCING the failure the seat feared. (1) EDITQUALITY (high, gating) — 'a jsonb = against a missing key evaluates NULL so the RAISE never fires': the verify block does NOT use a bare comparison-and-branch; it uses PERFORM … WHERE <jsonb comparisons> then IF NOT FOUND THEN RAISE — a NULL comparison excludes the row, NOT FOUND goes true, the RAISE fires. PROVEN BY INDUCTION, not argument: in a transaction I moved output_field back into config on the LIVE row (jsonb_set / #- exactly reproducing the regression), ran the identical DO block, and it raised 'ASSERT FIRED CORRECTLY on the induced regression'; transaction rolled back, live config untouched. The check fails closed. (2) EDITQUALITY (medium, recurrenceExpected) — the seat's feared 'third occurrence silently swallowed' does not exist in the mechanism as written: writeWorkItem's strike counter counts only TERMINAL same-key predecessors (status IN ('complete','failed'), 7-day window); a still-OPEN orphan item is dedup-suppressed by the ON CONFLICT clause, which is not a strike; the within-cycle suppression window is <3h and the scan cadence is 6h, so it cannot bite; and the third filing after two closes is INSERTED with status 'unresolved' — visible, and 'unresolved' is in workItemRevalidatableStatuses so the RFC_010 revalidation sweep can close it on positive re-observation. Nothing is swallowed at this cadence. (3) EDITQUALITY (low) + PRIOR_ART (low) — thunderAdapterTopic: grep shows exactly one declaration (thunder_decommission_dispatch.go:38, package-level const); thunder_list_dispatch.go references it without redeclaring; the package compiles at HEAD, which for a Go const collision is the proof. (4) REUSE_AGENT (medium) — why a separate agent rather than extending thunder-reaper: the reaper is a pre_query-driven dispatcher over OUR thunder_instances table, and a scheduler pre_query is SQL — it structurally cannot call the vendor API, which is the only place an orphan is visible; the orphan scan exists precisely for the blindness the reaper's mechanism cannot escape. They also differ in cadence (900s vs 6h) and workflow shape (single fire-and-forget dispatch vs dispatch→await→reconcile). They deliberately SHARE the thunder-lifecycle concurrency group so they never interleave. The reaper's own inert config-nested output_field is left unfixed on purpose: nothing reads its response, so the fix would be cosmetic churn on a working pipeline — the trap is recorded as a LANDMINES entry (verifier dispatched) instead, which protects every FUTURE copier, not just this one. (5) GUARDIAN (medium) — system.internal confirmed by direct SQL this round: sites row eac60db8-b032-432b-b36d-76f37632045d, domain system.internal, status system. (6) DEBUG_HISTORIAN (medium, advisory) — 'was the hardened file actually re-applied or only checksum-synced': confirmed by reading the LIVE row this round: agent_definitions carries step-level output_field on BOTH steps (dispatch_list→thunder_list, reconcile→reconcile_result) and the config-nested key is ABSENT; scheduled_tasks shows enabled/21600/thunder-lifecycle/no-pre_query. The ledger checksum matches the file as applied. (7) PRIOR_ART (medium, advisory) — liveness claims a council tier cannot corroborate: acknowledged as the protocol requires. The pod-grep commands for a human re-run are in the submission verbatim (grounded_in), and the 24h orchestration retention caveat is accepted: the COMPLETED run's counts are durably recorded in the lane NOTES and the register entry, so an empty orchestration_states read later is retention, not refutation.
